messages:
maria: saw a 3x tail-latency spike on eu-west dedicated handoffs at ~08:12 UTC, correlated with a bunch of small carve-in requests
devops_alex: looked at traces — handoff path goes eu-west->controlplane->eu2-proxy today due to capacity shortfall, adds ~120ms
sre_jin: logs show queuing at proxy: `proxy_queue_len` jumped from 20->190 for 90s, CPU at 85% on the proxy pod
maria: that's the pattern. before we did soft-fallback to nearest compatible pool, now fallback picks remote compatible and we get net latency + jitter
ryan: is this the same as the 'fallback routing weight' change from last week? I bumped the prefer-local threshold to 0.6

devops_alex: yep, after the threshold change we started preferring capacity-compat over locality, which reduces OOMs but increases handoff distance for tiny carve-ins

maria: cost vs latency tradeoff. customers on dedicated slices hit 95th p99 > SLO briefly. Need quick mitigation for next hour

sre_jin: temporary mitigation proposals:
- revert prefer-local threshold -> prefer locality
- add short-circuit for carve-ins < 30s to stay local or queue into warm pool
- route small carve-ins through regional proxy with fast-path

maria: reversion is simplest. downside: may raise preemptions and OOMs for noisy ephemeral tenants

ryan: could we instead change the handoff decision to prefer locality only when predicted request length < 200 tokens? cheaper than blunt revert

devops_alex: doable. prediction model available via lightweight classifier. quick patch:

``` 
if predicted_len < 200 and pool_local_score > 0.4:
    prefer_local = true
else:
    prefer_local = pool_compatibility > 0.7
```

sre_jin: rolling that patch to staging now, will watch proxy_queue_len and p99 latencies

infra-bot: deploy started: handoff-routing-fastpath v2 -> canary on eu-west (1/3 proxies)

maria: monitoring dashboards -> watching p95/p99, proxy_queue_len, kvcache_hitrate

ryan: heads-up on cost: keeping more carve-ins local bumps utilization variance, might increase reserved pool need over time. we'll need a short report if we keep it post-mitigation

sre_jin: canary looks good so far, p99 dropped from 420ms->180ms on canary proxies, queue_len capped at 35

devops_alex: rolling to remaining eu-west proxies in 6m if signals hold

maria: thanks team. after roll I'll spin up a follow-up doc: small-carvein-routing-proposal with longterm tradeoffs (cost accounting + soft-isolation knobs)

ryan: add a runbook note: when controlplane indicates cross-region fallback >5% disable long-run local-preference for this region

maria: agreed. I'll create the runbook entry and ping infra on-call for the change window
sre_jin: postmortem ticket created: INFRA-7991
maria: closing thread, will update when doc is live :thumbsup:
